newsitem.title: TAIWAN: ADB's T$7 bln Taiwan-dollar bond coupon 6.00 pct.
newsitem.headline: ADB's T$7 bln Taiwan-dollar bond coupon 6.00 pct.

text.p: The coupon rate for the Asian Development Bank's T$7 billion Taiwan dollar-denominated bond was set on Thursday at 6.00 percent, lead underwriter ChinaTrust Commercial Bank said.
The Asian Development Bank decided the bond, its second denominated in Taiwan currency, would be a seven-year issue, the ChinaTrust official said.
Taiwan's central bank in early November approved the ADB's latest application to issue a bond to raise T$7 billion, or US$255 million, in Taiwan's liquidity-rich money market.
ADB initially had scheduled a June launch for a 10-year, US$200 million issue, but it later postponed the issue without giving a reason.
Taiwan's central bank has said the ADB Taiwan cash call would help internationalise the island's bond market and raise the international credibility of Taiwan's currency.
In August 1995, the ADB issued a seven-year Taiwan dollar-denominated bond valued at T$2.6 billion, or roughly US$100 million.
